clue.text: Box, almost free

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: spare as in free or unoccupied, like spare time

explanation.surface: Someone notes a box going nearly for nothing at a sale.
explanation.definitionFit: To spar is to box, especially in practice bouts with a partner.

clue.text: One going into storyline for trial episode

indicators.note: going into places one piece inside another, which surrounds it

parts.note: the plot is the storyline
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A character is written into the storyline of a test episode of a TV series.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot is a single trial episode made to test whether a television series is worth commissioning.

clue.text: Unkempt woman in plant

parts.note: ragged means scruffy or unkempt
a lady is a woman

explanation.surface: A dishevelled woman is spotted lurking among the greenery.
explanation.walkthrough: Ragged lady is a garden flower, Nigella damascena, also called love-in-a-mist.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragged lady is a common name for love-in-a-mist, a garden flower with feathery leaves.

clue.text: Very high, one girl backing singer outside

indicators.note: outside means the singer surrounds the rest, sitting on both sides of it

parts.note: an alto is a singer of the lower female or high male range
the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: backing means going in the opposite direction, so the word is read right to left

parts.note: a miss is a girl or young woman

explanation.surface: A girl provides very high backing vocals for a lead singer.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed girl follows the one, and both sit inside the singer, between ALT and O.
explanation.definitionFit: Altissimo is the musical term for the register above the treble stave, so very high in pitch.

clue.text: Author's horny tale — no plot involved

indicators.note: involved means complicated or tangled, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: fifteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A reviewer complains that a writer's racy story has no plot to speak of.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that the decorous Victorian novelist of the Barsetshire books is the last writer to produce a horny tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Trollope was a prolific Victorian novelist, author of Barchester Towers and The Way We Live Now.

clue.text: Novel youth politics Herod concocted involving sons

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so an extra letter is drawn into the mix
something concocted is cooked up from ingredients, so the letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: eighteen letters to rearrange
S is the standard abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A novel in which Herod stirs up youth politics, with his sons drawn in.
explanation.walkthrough: Herod famously killed his own sons, which suits the surface; the son's letter joins the other eighteen before they are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The Old Curiosity Shop is the Dickens novel featuring Little Nell and her grandfather.

clue.text: See 5
Individuals entering country, a republic

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so the first word is placed within the second

parts.note: the South Asian country
individuals taken one at a time are ones

explanation.surface: People entering a country find it is a republic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'country, a republic' reads as one definition, but country is wordplay and only 'a republic' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Indonesia is a presidential republic in Southeast Asia, made up of thousands of islands.

clue.text: Colombian painter born in a state on the Pacific

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the name of the state

parts.note: a US state on the Pacific coast
B is the abbreviation for born, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A Colombian artist was born in a coastal American state.
explanation.definitionFit: Alejandro Obregón was a leading twentieth-century Colombian painter, known for works such as Violencia.

clue.text: Female with instrument that's easy to carry in a black box?

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for female
something light is easy to carry
the recorder is a woodwind instrument

explanation.surface: A woman has a portable musical instrument kept in a black case.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'black box' is not a case but the aviation device; the light piece sits between the female and the instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The flight recorder on an aircraft is popularly called the black box, though it is usually orange.

clue.text: Stud manager

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a raised knob or ornamental stud
second meaning: the person in charge at work

explanation.surface: The person who runs a horse-breeding stud.
explanation.walkthrough: Stud suggests horses, but it means a raised ornamental knob.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a round projecting knob on a shield or surface and an informal term for an employer.

clue.text: Active, new hotline box office installed

indicators.note: installed means put in place inside, so the abbreviation is taken into the mix
new suggests a fresh version, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
BO is the standard abbreviation for box office

explanation.surface: A theatre box office has a brand new hotline up and running.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on the boil is in an active state, still being worked on, like a pot kept bubbling.

clue.text: Horse meeting second hurdle

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
a nag is an old or poor horse

explanation.surface: A racehorse at a race meeting faces the second hurdle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meeting' sounds like a race meeting, but it only means the two pieces join, the second going first.
explanation.definitionFit: A snag is an obstacle or problem, and a hurdle in the figurative sense is the same.

clue.text: Scottish town eerie in low light

indicators.note: eerie means strange or weird, so the following letters take a strange new order

parts.note: ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A Scottish town looks spooky in the dusk.
explanation.definitionFit: Linlithgow is a town in West Lothian, Scotland, known for its ruined royal palace.

clue.text: Rehearsed moves in Macbeth, say, on stage

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing on another means it comes after it, so the play is sent second

parts.note: the set is the stage scenery for a production
Macbeth is an example of a play

explanation.surface: Actors practise their moves for Macbeth on the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: In football, a set play is a practised move from a free kick or corner; the theatrical surface hides that sporting sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A set play is a pre-planned routine from a dead-ball situation in football or rugby, worked out in training.

clue.text: Thieves duck coming to part of roof that sticks out

parts.note: the teal is a small duck

parts.words: part of roof that sticks out
parts.note: the eaves are the overhanging edge of a roof

explanation.surface: Burglars and a duck both end up perched on the roof overhang.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang: tea leaves rhymes with thieves, so it means thieves.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cockney rhyming slang tea leaves stands for thieves, often shortened to tea leaf for a single thief.

clue.text: Deep red lips included in deception

indicators.note: included in places one word inside the other

parts.note: a con is a trick or deception
lips in the sense of edges or rims

explanation.surface: Bright red lipstick is part of a disguise.
explanation.walkthrough: Lips points to mouths, but here it means edges, as the lip of a cup.
explanation.definitionFit: Crimson is a deep, rich shade of red tending towards purple.

clue.text: Drowned youth's name used in editorial

indicators.note: used in puts the abbreviation inside the other word

parts.note: a newspaper's leader is its editorial
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A newspaper editorial names a young man who drowned.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Leander swam the Hellespont nightly to meet Hero and drowned in a storm.
explanation.definitionFit: Leander is the young lover from Greek legend who drowned crossing the Hellespont to reach Hero.

clue.text: Hated to charge to store article

indicators.note: to store means to keep something inside, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: to charge a gun or a cart is to load it
the definite article

explanation.surface: Someone hated being asked to pay to keep a piece of property in storage.
explanation.definitionFit: Loathed is the past tense of loathe, to hate intensely.

clue.text: Issue concerning tenancy agreement

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a lease is a tenancy agreement

explanation.surface: A dispute about a rental agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' looks like a noun meaning a problem, but it is the verb meaning to put out.
explanation.definitionFit: To release a record or statement is to issue it, put it out publicly.

clue.text: Organ, new make

parts.note: the ear is an organ of hearing
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A shopper asks about a new brand of church organ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make' looks like a noun for a brand, but it is the verb, as in to make money.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a living or a sum of money is to earn it.

clue.text: Take off before ten for summit

parts.note: to ape someone is to mimic or take them off
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: Climbers set off before ten in the morning to reach the summit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take off' suggests departing, but here it means imitate; 'before' places it ahead of the numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: The apex is the highest point or tip of something, the same as its summit.

clue.text: Circus performer working with pride

parts.note: surface reading: an entertainer who takes pride in the job
setter's reading: a pride is a group of lions, the animals this performer handles

explanation.walkthrough: Pride seems to mean self-respect, but it is the collective noun for big cats.
explanation.definitionFit: This circus artiste works in the ring with a group of big cats, training them to perform.

clue.text: Civic head in Irish county close to border

parts.note: County Mayo is in the west of Ireland

indicators.note: close to means at the end of a word, so only its last letter counts

parts.note: the final letter of border

explanation.surface: A local official in an Irish county near the border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to border' reads as near the frontier, but it means the end of the word border.
explanation.definitionFit: The mayor is the elected head of a town or city council, its civic leader.

clue.text: A long way, old European port

parts.note: far means a long way off
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: An old European port lies a long way off.
explanation.definitionFit: Faro is a port city on the Algarve coast of southern Portugal.

clue.text: Act like a rake in need of ocular treatment?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a rake is a womaniser, whose attention keeps wandering to other people
second meaning, taken literally: an eye that wanders out of line, a medical complaint

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase for a flirt's wandering attention is read literally as an eye that will not stay put.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with a wandering eye is habitually attracted to people other than their partner, as a rake or libertine is.

clue.text: Find nightclub ideal

parts.note: a disco is a nightclub for dancing
as in 'the very thing', meaning exactly right or ideal

explanation.surface: Someone finds the perfect nightclub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Find' looks like a verb, but it is the noun, a thing found.
explanation.definitionFit: A discovery is a find, something newly come upon or uncovered.

clue.text: Friendly member accompanying wife

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for wife
a member is a limb, such as an arm

explanation.surface: A sociable club member arrives with his wife.
explanation.definitionFit: A warm welcome or manner is a friendly, affectionate one.
